- When sentiment is negative and forecast is below recent low, model tends to undercorrect — adjust upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- If forecast shows sharp spike followed by high values, model often overshoots — cap peak forecasts or reduce slope after spike.
- In mean-reverting regimes (sentiment neutral or mildly negative), model overpredicts mean — reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent average to align with reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative and price is falling, model often fails to anticipate further drop — add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast tail.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate volatility in early period — smooth initial forecast values toward historical mean.
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often overestimates momentum — reduce forecast slope or cap growth rate at 1.5–2% per day.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model exhibits lag — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment shift.
